# Design System

> Design system for generating consistent user interfaces from Figma designs using AI coding assistants such as Cursor.

## Instructions

* Follow `AGENTS.md` for project rules and implementation guidelines.
* Follow `Source_of_truth.md` when sources conflict.
* Follow `DESIGN.md` for general design-system usage rules.
* Use existing component metadata and design tokens instead of inventing new styles.
* Preserve the visual design, spacing, typography, colors, and component states defined in Figma.
* Reuse existing components whenever possible.

## Component Metadata

* Component schema: `component.schema.json`
* Component definitions: `components/`
* Semantic docs (optional companion files): `*.docs.yaml` alongside Specs YAML

### Components (Specs keys → file)

| Specs key     | File                          |
|---------------|-------------------------------|
| button        | `components/button.yaml`      |
| RadioButton   | `components/RadioButton.yaml` |
| checkbox      | `components/checkbox.yaml`    |
| input         | `components/input.yaml`       |
| link          | `components/link.yaml`        |
| tab           | `components/tab.yaml`         |
| tag           | `components/tag.yaml`         |
| blockHeader   | `components/blockHeader.yaml` |

Do not invent alternate filenames (`links.yaml`, `tags.yaml`, etc.). Use the names above.

## Design Tokens

* Token definitions: `tokens/tokens.json`
* Use semantic tokens when available.
* Do not introduce arbitrary colors, spacing, typography, or border-radius values when existing tokens apply.

## Accessibility

* Requirements: `accessibility.yaml` (WCAG 2.2 AA)
* Apply component-specific rules for button, input, checkbox, RadioButton, tab, link, tag, and blockHeader.

## Figma

* Figma is the source of truth for visual design, component appearance, layout, and variants.
* Component metadata documents available properties, states, and intended usage.
* Follow the existing Figma component structure and reuse available assets.

## AI Implementation Guidelines

* Inspect the existing project structure before generating code.
* Reuse documented components and tokens.
* Match the Figma layout as closely as possible.
* Do not create duplicate components when an existing component can be reused.
* If a required component, property, or token is missing, identify the gap before introducing a new pattern.
* Validate the generated interface against the original design.
* Never claim sources are synchronized unless synchronization was actually verified.

## Current Goal

Generate working user interfaces from Figma designs while maintaining consistency with the existing design system.
